[MUQATIL:17:9-11/r3] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The person praying for evil against himself is al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, who demanded punishment in 8:32, just as people pray for good for themselves. | mentions 8:32
[MUQATIL:17:9-11/r4] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Human haste is illustrated by Adam trying to sit when the spirit had reached only his middle, before reaching his feet; al-Nadr similarly hastened his self-directed curse, and humanity inherited haste from Adam.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In doubled roots of the waw class, two waw radicals are not retained; speakers choose forms that turn one waw into yāʾ, avoiding the disliked sequence.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | ارعويت retains its first waw because the imperfect does not change it; it cannot be turned into alif before a consonant, as with نزوان.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The augmented pattern from حييت follows the same rules as the pattern from رميت.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The pattern افعللت from حييت behaves like اقتتل: its medial yāʾs may be assimilated, pronounced clearly, or concealed according to the corresponding اقتتل variants.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r13] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Medial doubled letters resist the treatment of final geminates because their position is stronger, so اقتتلوا does not assimilate like رددت.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r14] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Augmented forms from a double-waw root follow غزوت: speakers say احواوت and احواويت, with the waw corresponding to the waw of غزوت.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r15] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In احواويت the verbal noun احوياء has yāʾ replacing waw, as in the change in أيام.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r16] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | When the two waws are medial in احوييت, they remain because medial doubling is stronger, like the internal sequence in اقتتلنا.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r17] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The medial form احوويت follows اقتتلت; its verbal noun is احوواء, parallel to قتال, while the other form yields حواء.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r18] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The form of شويت is شي: waw becomes yāʾ when quiescent before yāʾ, and the preceding consonant takes kasra to avoid ḍamma with yāʾ.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r19] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · بعض العرب | reports | Some Arabs use an initial ḍamma in this form: after assimilation removes the length, it resembles صيد rather than بيض or forms with a medial radical.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Forms such as قويت and حويت show the change: the original middle radical makes the final waw into yāʾ, with kasra before it.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r20] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The rhyme comparison with عمي shows this form is not like بيض; it is also unlike the medial consonants in عتي، عصي، and مسنية.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r21] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · العرب | reports | Sībawayh reports the expressions قرن ألوى and قرون لي as attested forms illustrating the comparison.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r22] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | ريا and رية have a waw substituted for hamza and follow the pattern of شويت; some speakers also pronounce the forms with kasra like لي.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r23] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · من قال ريا | reports | Those who say ريا with kasra pronounce وي with kasra too, except in the expression إسادة.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r24] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · يونس | reports | The regular form is معاي; معايا is also used by analogy with مدارى and صحارى because yāʾ is especially burdensome by itself.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r25] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | لم أبل derives from باليت; jussive sukun causes deletion of the alif to avoid two consecutive quiescent letters, and the root yāʾ is then deleted as in يكن.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r26] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | These deletions are favored by frequency and are irregular, not productive; Sībawayh compares them with omitted nūn in يكن and forms like منذ from لدن.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r27] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | Khalil reports an alternative لم أبله, with only the alif deleted; frequent deletion is compared with the lost alif in أحمر and علبط and waw in غد.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r28] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | ما أباليه بالة is treated as though it were بالية, by analogy with عافية.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r29] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | They retain the alif in لا أبالي because the form is strong and does not require deletion; alif is omitted only where the vowel is deleted, such as in the jussive.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | They do not say قووت تقوو like غزوت تغزو because the doubled articulation is lighter with one tongue lift, as in سال and راس.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A single word does not combine waw as first and final radicals, as shown by the absent وعوت; the sequence is disfavored even where doubling is common.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Yāʾ can occur as both first and final radicals, as in يديت إليه يدا, but this is less common; repeated waw is allowed in quadriliteral forms such as الوزوزة and الوحوحة.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Repeated waw and hamza occur in quadriliteral reduplicatives because this pattern is frequent and the repeated letters are separated; waw is easier than hamza.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The augmented patterns from رميت parallel أحييت in assimilation, clear pronunciation, and concealment; Sībawayh lists corresponding imperfect, imperative, and verbal-noun forms.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The concealment variant in the رميت paradigm follows whichever pronunciation speakers use for يحييان.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالتضعيففيبناتالواو)#797/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Augmented forms from غزوت are اغزويت and اغزاويت; they do not assimilate or conceal because no two same-place letters meet.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحروفالستةإذاكانواحدمنهاعيناوكانتالفاءقبلها#711/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | When the second radical is one of the six gutturals, four vowel patterns are regular across verbs, nouns, and adjectives; faʿīl also has two patterns.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحروفالستةإذاكانواحدمنهاعيناوكانتالفاءقبلها#711/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | أجيء and similar forms follow the regular pattern they would have if completed, since the letter after the pattern's alif is inherently unvocalized.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحروفالستةإذاكانواحدمنهاعيناوكانتالفاءقبلها#711/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · تميم | reports | Tamim breaks the first radical with kasra in these forms when the second radical is one of the six gutturals.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحروفالستةإذاكانواحدمنهاعيناوكانتالفاءقبلها#711/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The gutturals affect the imperfect pattern; the first radical takes kasra because the form requires it, and this light vowel keeps the articulation simple.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحروفالستةإذاكانواحدمنهاعيناوكانتالفاءقبلها#711/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · أهل الحجاز | reports | The Hijaz dialect applies the regular analogy to all these forms.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحروفالستةإذاكانواحدمنهاعيناوكانتالفاءقبلها#711/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Both رؤف and رؤوف occur; the waw does not govern the vowel across the greater distance from alif, unlike the closer yāʾ.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحروفالستةإذاكانواحدمنهاعيناوكانتالفاءقبلها#711/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · بعض العرب | reports | Some Arabs pronounce بئيس without realizing the hamza, leaving the remaining form intact, as in their lightening of شهد.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحروفالستةإذاكانواحدمنهاعيناوكانتالفاءقبلها#711/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | مغيرة and معين result from vowel assimilation, with one kasra following another, as in منتن and the cited forms for أجيئك and أنبئك.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحروفالستةإذاكانواحدمنهاعيناوكانتالفاءقبلها#711/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The anomalous إحب، نحب، and يحب follow the pattern of منتن even though حببت is not used.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحروفالستةإذاكانواحدمنهاعيناوكانتالفاءقبلها#711/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Some imperfect forms follow a pattern whose perfect is unattested: يدع and يذر are treated as if ودعت and وذرت existed, a usage supported by their frequency.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءعلىأنفعلتمنهمثلبعتوإنكانلميستعملفيالكلام#796/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | For a root such as حي, retaining both yāʾs in the imperfect would produce an unacceptable form; deleting one instead creates ambiguity with يعي and يقي, so the compounded defect is avoided.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءعلىأنفعلتمنهمثلبعتوإنكانلميستعملفيالكلام#796/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | حيوة is treated as deriving from an unattested حيوت; speakers avoid a quiescent waw before yāʾ where the yāʾ is not stable through the verb's forms.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءعلىأنفعلتمنهمثلبعتوإنكانلميستعملفيالكلام#796/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The sequence is tolerated in لويت because its waw remains present in يلوي, unlike the unstable sequence in يوجل, whose waw shifts to yāʾ.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءعلىأنفعلتمنهمثلبعتوإنكانلميستعملفيالكلام#796/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | آي، غاية، and آية are exceptional forms on the pattern of بعت alth
